Subject: Request: temporary snapshot staging hold for Acme Health migration

Hi Kimberly,

We have a scheduled migration this month and our auditors asked us to retain a recent set of system snapshots for 30 days beyond our planned purge window to validate integrity during the cutover. The snapshots are from the week of Oct 22-29 and contain operational logs for a limited set of customer IDs.

Can Redwood pause the automated backup purge for these snapshot prefixes and mark them as "staging-retain" for 30 days? We can provide a manifest (attached) with the exact snapshot IDs and a short justification note for our compliance team.

If there are contractual or DPA implications, please let me know what information you need — we can have Legal follow up.

Attachments: acme_snapshot_manifest.csv (CSV list of snapshot IDs and retention window)

Thanks,
Sarah

Acme Health

Kimberly — thanks for flagging. Technical notes and proposal below.

Summary of approach (low-risk):
1) Create a short-lived staging tag (metadata key: retention_exception=acme_migration_202811) on each snapshot listed in their manifest.
2) Exempt those blobs from the nightly purge job for 14 days (config flip + audit entry).
3) At exception end, run a verification pass, then let normal purge proceed; if Acme requests extension, we require signed addendum and ops approval.

Work estimate: ~2 engineer-days to implement tagging and gated-exempt flow (includes rollout to canary + metrics). Rollback: remove tag and resume purge immediately; we keep logs of all actions.

Operational safeguards:
- Limit scope to the exact snapshot IDs in attached manifest.
- Audit log entry with operator and timestamp; retention of logs for 90 days.
- Automatic expiry of the staging tag after N days to avoid indefinite holds.

Attachments: dpa_request_form.pdf (blank DPA addendum form we can use for signatures)

I'll draft the ops checklist once legal confirms the acceptability of a time-limited exception.

- Aditya

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Nov 2028 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FWD: Request: temporary snapshot staging hold for Acme Health migration

Thanks — I reviewed. Legal position and required checklist:

Legal position:
- We can permit a short, documented retention exception for specific snapshot IDs for operational validation purposes provided we have: a signed DPA addendum (or email confirmation from an authorized signatory) that amends the retention/purge schedule; and a clear expiration date.

Required checklist before exception is granted:
1) Signed DPA addendum or a DocuSign envelope opened for the addendum (we should not rely on informal email approvals).
2) Manifest file that exactly lists snapshot IDs (we have this).
3) Scope limit in writing: what data classes are involved (PHI? personal identifiers?) — Acme to confirm.
4) Ops runbook describing how the exception is applied and how automatic expiry is enforced.
5) A named Redwood operator and an internal ticket for audit trail.

Recommendation: grant a 14-day exception by default (not 30) unless Acme signs the addendum requesting a longer period and provides justification tied to a compliance obligation. Shorter period reduces risk and operational exposure.

If Legal gets the signed addendum, we can process a one-time extension, documented and logged. Jordan

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Nov 2028 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Request: temporary snapshot staging hold for Acme Health migration

Hi Sarah — thanks for the manifest. We can support a temporary staging hold while you complete your validation, but we need to align on process and minimal paperwork.

What we will do (operational):
- Apply a time-bound "staging-retain" tag to the exact snapshot IDs you provided and exempt them from automated purge for 14 days starting 2028-11-13 00:00:00 UTC.
- Redwood will log the operator, write an audit entry, and enforce automatic expiry so the snapshots are eligible for purge on 2028-11-27 00:00:00 UTC unless an approved extension is in place.
- Our engineering team (Aditya) will implement the tag and guard in a canary region first and then run a verification job.

What we need from Acme (next steps):
1) Please have an authorized signatory for Acme Health execute the DPA addendum we sent via DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/ACME-DPA-ADDENDUM-12345 . We can accept a signed DocuSign or an email from an authorized corporate counsel confirming the request and timeframe.
2) Confirm whether the snapshots contain PHI or other regulated data so Legal can finalize the addendum language.
3) Confirm who at Acme will be the primary contact for extensions (name, title, email).

Attachments referenced: acme_snapshot_manifest.csv, dpa_request_form.pdf

If we receive the signed addendum by EOD Monday (2028-11-13), we'll proceed with the 14-day staging hold on schedule. If not, we can still grant a narrower, 72-hour operational hold as a fallback while paperwork completes.

Best,
Kimberly Park
